qa_pairs.question: According to the chart of the new economy scale and its proportion in GDP, as well as the chart of the growth rate of the digital economy and GDP, what might be the main reasons for the continuous increase in the proportion of the new economy in GDP?

answer.A: In 2016, the growth rate of the digital economy was lower than that of GDP, but the proportion of the new economy still increased, indicating that other factors such as the influencer economy drove it (wrong interpretation: in 2016, the growth rate of the digital economy was 18.9% > the growth rate of GDP was 6.8%, with a significant gap).
answer.B: Due to the strong support of government policies for the new economy sector, its scale has expanded rapidly, thus increasing its proportion in GDP (not relying on the chart, only based on common sense).
answer.C: The annual growth rate of the new economy scale may generally be higher than that of GDP, which can be inferred from the comparison of growth rates and is the key factor for the continuous increase in the proportion.
answer.D: Even in the years when the overall economy slowed down, the growth rate of the digital economy remained relatively high, helping the new economy maintain its growth momentum and leading to an increase in the proportion.
answer.E: The continuous shrinkage of traditional economic sectors such as manufacturing has made room for the new economy, indirectly pushing up its proportion (based on industry common sense, without involving chart data).
answer.F: In 2020, the GDP growth rate was relatively high (2.2%), but the growth rate of the digital economy was only slightly higher (9.7%), which was not enough to explain the increase in the proportion (wrong comparison: in 2020, the actual GDP growth rate was extremely low, and the growth rate of the digital economy was more than four times that of GDP).
answer.G: The growth rate of the digital economy was significantly higher than that of GDP in most years, which may have driven the expansion of the new economy scale, thus increasing its proportion in GDP.

qa_pairs.question: In 2020, the GDP growth rate dropped significantly to a low level, but the proportion of the new economy in GDP increased instead. answer.A: In 2020, the growth rate of the digital economy (9.7%) was lower than that of the influencer economy (15.9%), but both were lower than the GDP growth rate (2.2%), which could not explain the increase in the proportion (wrong interpretation: the growth rate of the digital economy was 9.7% > the growth rate of GDP was 2.2%, and the influencer economy was even higher at 15.9%).

answer.D: The growth rate of the influencer economy remained at a relatively high level in 2020, which may have partially offset the shrinkage of the traditional economy and helped the new economy maintain its performance.
answer.E: Although the growth rate of the digital economy decreased, it was still much higher than that of GDP, which may have supported the relative growth of the new economy scale, leading to an increase in the proportion.
answer.F: The new economy sectors (such as the digital and influencer economies) showed stronger resilience when the overall economy slowed down, and their growth rate advantages may jointly explain the increase in the proportion.
answer.G: The traditional economy was more affected by supply - chain disruptions, while the new economy was relatively immune (using industry common sense, without involving chart comparison).
